In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PDGFRs may be involved in the differentiation of eosinophiles in CBF leukemia, but not in leukemogenesis.

the FIP1 PDGFR fusion gene and the SNPs detected in the PDGFR JM and TK2 regions do not appear to be associated with the development of eosinophilia in CBF leukemia, but rather with the development of the disease itself.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation of the PDGF signaling pathway may be linked to the differentiation of eosinophiles in CBF leukemia, however, the activation of the pathway does not seem to play a significant role in leukemogenesis of AML with CBF abnormalities.
the expression of the Fip1 like 1 Platelet derived growth receptor a fusion gene is not found in CBF leukemias.
PDGFRa or b is not a good target for therapy in patients with CBF leukemia with or without eosinophilia, and that the PDGFR inhibitors are unlikely to be useful in this setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of PDGFR genes is not associated with the presence of eosinophilia or the leukemogenic potential of the disease.

the FIP1 L1/PDGFRa fusion gene is not involved in CBF leukemia and that the PDGFR genes are expressed in all CBF leukemia with or without eosinophilia, but no genetic abnormality of the PDGFRA/B genes is found.
